subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LAN stand for?
questions.explain: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small geographical area such as a single site or building.

questions.q: In a star topology, every device is connected to a single central device. What is this central device typically?
questions.explain: In a star topology each node connects to a central switch (or hub) that directs data between devices.

questions.q: The Internet is best described as which type of network?
questions.explain: The Internet is a Wide Area Network (WAN) because it spans a very large geographical area.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a mesh topology over a star topology?
options: If one connection fails, data can be rerouted along another path
It requires far less cabling to set up
All data must pass through a single central switch
It is always cheaper to install
questions.explain: Because devices have multiple connections, a mesh has no single point of failure and can reroute data.

questions.q: Which of the following would most directly improve the performance of a network by allowing more data to be transmitted per second?
options: A higher number of simultaneous users
questions.explain: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be transmitted per second, so greater bandwidth improves performance.

questions.q: In a client-server network, where are shared files and resources centrally stored and managed?
questions.explain: In a client-server model the server centrally stores, manages and provides resources to the client devices.

questions.q: In a star network, the single cable connecting one computer to the central switch is accidentally cut. What is the most likely effect?
options: Only that one computer loses its network connection
Every computer loses its connection to the switch
Data is automatically rerouted so nothing is affected
questions.explain: In a star topology each device has its own cable, so a single break only isolates that one device.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of DNS (the Domain Name System)?
options: To translate domain names into IP addresses
To encrypt data sent over the Internet
To split data into packets for transmission
To assign MAC addresses to devices
questions.explain: DNS resolves human-readable domain names (e.g. bbc.co.uk) into the IP addresses computers use to locate servers.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to send email from a client to a mail server?
questions.explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email, while IMAP is used to retrieve it.

questions.q: How many layers are there in the TCP/IP model used in the AQA specification?
questions.explain: The TCP/IP model has four layers: application, transport, internet (network) and link (data link).

questions.q: Which statement best describes a MAC address?
options: A unique physical address assigned to a network interface card
An address that changes each time a device joins a network
A name that is translated by DNS into an IP address
A protocol used to transfer web pages
questions.explain: A MAC address is a unique hardware (physical) address permanently assigned to a device's network interface card.

questions.q: How does HTTPS differ from HTTP?
options: HTTPS encrypts the data sent between the browser and the server
HTTPS transfers files faster than HTTP
HTTPS does not require an IP address
HTTPS is only used for sending email
questions.explain: HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP that encrypts communication so intercepted data cannot be read.

questions.q: What is the main role of the TCP protocol?
options: Splitting data into packets and reassembling them reliably at the destination
Translating domain names into IP addresses
Encrypting all data sent over a wireless network
Assigning physical addresses to network cards
questions.explain: TCP breaks data into numbered packets and ensures they are reassembled correctly and reliably at the receiver.

questions.q: In the four-layer TCP/IP model, at which layer does the HTTP protocol operate?
questions.explain: HTTP is an application-layer protocol, along with others such as HTTPS, FTP, SMTP and IMAP.

questions.q: A web developer needs to upload the files for a website onto a remote web server. Which protocol is most appropriate?
questions.explain: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is designed for transferring files between computers, such as uploading to a server.

questions.q: What does the term 'malware' mean?
options: Malicious software designed to damage or gain access to a system
A physical fault in network cabling
questions.explain: Malware is malicious software (such as viruses, worms or trojans) created to harm or gain unauthorised access to systems.

questions.q: Sending a fake email pretending to be from a bank to trick a user into revealing their password is an example of which type of attack?
questions.explain: Phishing manipulates people into giving away confidential information, which is a form of social engineering.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a firewall?
options: To monitor and filter traffic entering and leaving a network
To translate domain names into IP addresses
To physically lock server room doors
questions.explain: A firewall inspects incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks anything that does not meet its security rules.

questions.q: An attacker types database commands into a website's login box to try to read data from its database. What kind of attack is this?
questions.explain: SQL injection enters malicious SQL through an input field to manipulate or extract data from a database.

questions.q: A company employs security specialists to deliberately attack its own network to find weaknesses before real criminals do. What is this process called?
questions.explain: Penetration testing simulates attacks on a system to identify and fix vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.
